UPSTREAM: media: uvcvideo: queue: Support asynchronous buffer handling The buffer queue interface currently operates sequentially, processing buffers after they have fully completed. In preparation for supporting parallel tasks operating on the buffers, we will need to support buffers being processed on multiple CPUs. Adapt the uvc_queue_next_buffer() such that a reference count tracks the active use of the buffer, returning the buffer to the VB2 stack at completion. UPSTREAM: media: uvcvideo: Abstract streaming object lifetime The streaming object is a key part of handling the UVC device. Although not critical, we are currently missing a call to destroy the mutex on clean up paths, and we are due to extend the objects complexity in the near future. Facilitate easy management of a stream object by creating a pair of functions to handle creating and destroying the allocation. The new uvc_stream_delete() function also performs the missing mutex_destroy() operation. Previously a failed streaming object allocation would cause uvc_parse_streaming() to return -EINVAL, which is inappropriate. If the constructor failes, we will instead return -ENOMEM. While we're here, fix the trivial spelling error in the function banner of uvc_delete(). power: Set the default keyboard wakeup capability to enabled. As part of crrev.com/c/1069220, we deleted the udev rule that tries to control the wakeup capability of internal keyboard. The reason for the change was powerd and EC seem to get into a race to control wakes from internal keyboard. Please look at crbug.com/836279 for more details. After this change powerd stopped worrying abount internal keyboard. This will be a problem if the default value of power/wakeup property of the internal keyboard is set to disabled for 2 reasons. 1. If the default state is disabled, and if the user presses a key when the kernel is in the suspend path, power core in the kernel will not abort the suspend. 2. Dark resume will not work as we cannot attribute wakeups to keybaord since the wakeup count will not increment if the property is set to disabled. To fix this on the ARM side, we set the default state to enabled(crrev.com/c/1101959). On the intel side we use atkbd driver, which is a generic driver. I highly doubt a patch to set the default state will be accepted. Thus instead set the default value to enabled in powerd. How was this not a problem on recent devices? It so happened that most of the devices that we build recently have side buttons. Thus we install a option udev rule 93-powerd-tags-keyboard-side-buttons.rules which enables wakeup. How was this not a problem on nocturne? Though nocturne does not have side buttons, nocturne does not use atkbd driver for internal keyboard. Since the internal keyboard is on usb bus, wake is enabled by default. Will this change cause any regressions on older devices? It should not. First on intel devices, only kernel honours this property. ACPI does not. Thus if keyboard causes any spurious wakes, previously device would end up in a suspend resume loop as kernel suspends and ec would wake the system immediately. Now the suspend fails. Thus the system would try for 10 times and shuts down instead. Thus this should only improve the situation. On ARM devices this property is set to enabled by default anyway. BUG=b:133262012 TEST=Run power_WakeSources and make sure the INTERNAL_KEYBOARD passes. FROMGIT: clk: rockchip: Remove 48 MHz PLL rate from rk3288 The 48 MHz PLL rate is not present in the downstream chromeos-3.14 tree. Looking at history, it was originally removed in <https://crrev.com/c/265810> ("CHROMIUM: clk: rockchip: expand more clocks support") with no explanation. Much of that patch was later reverted in <https://crrev.com/c/284595> ("CHROMIUM: clk: rockchip: Revert more questionable PLL rates"), but that patch left in the removal of 48 MHz. What I wrote in that patch: > Note that the original change also removed the rate (48000000, 1, > 64, 32) from the table. I have no idea why that was squashed in > there, but that rate was invalid anyway (it appears to have an out > of bounds NO). I'm not putting that rate in. Reading the TRM I see that NO is defined as - NO: 1, 2-16 (even only) ...and furthermore only 4 bits are assigned for NO-1, which means that the highest NO we could even represent is 16.
